prompt: A stop-and-wait sender transmits each frame quickly but waits much longer for its ACK. There is no loss. Why is most of the link's capacity unused?

options.text: The link cannot carry bits while an ACK is in flight under any protocol
options.explanation: Other protocols can pipeline more frames; the idling follows from stop-and-wait's one-outstanding-frame rule.

options.text: The frame's CRC forces the sender to pause for the whole route
options.explanation: The integrity check does not itself impose this one-frame feedback cycle.

options.text: The physical rate is too low to send a frame before feedback returns
options.explanation: The premise says frame transmission is short compared with the feedback interval.

options.text: The protocol allows no next frame until the previous acknowledgement arrives
options.explanation: Correct. The sender is idle for the long feedback interval even though it could physically send more.

workedExample: Trace one cycle: transmit one frame, then wait for its acknowledgement before sending the next. A long loss-free round trip therefore wastes time even without retransmissions. A sliding window can cover that interval with more outstanding frames, subject to its own buffering, sequence-number and recovery constraints.
